cases.question: The runner crosses the line of scrimmage, retreats behind it, and throws the first forward pass of the down. Is releasing it behind the line enough to make that pass legal?
answer_rubric: Answers no; once the ball crossed the line it cannot be brought back to enable a forward pass.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: The quarterback has been outside the pocket and, while under pressure, throws short of the line of scrimmage toward a realistic eligible receiver in the direction and vicinity of the pass. Does the short throw alone establish intentional grounding?
answer_rubric: Answers no; a realistic eligible receiver in direction and vicinity defeats the stated grounding condition.
Does not claim that the pass is legal in all other respects.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: An interior offensive lineman between the two ends wears an eligible number. Does that number alone make him an eligible receiver?
answer_rubric: Answers no; the interior alignment does not become eligible merely from an eligible number.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: A player with an ordinarily ineligible number reports as eligible, then aligns as an interior lineman between the two ends. Does reporting excuse that alignment?
answer_rubric: Answers no; reporting still requires an eligible position and legal formation.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: After the two-minute warning, a replay reversal corrects a ruling to one that would have left the clock running. Can the defense decline that replay runoff?
answer_rubric: Answers no; neither team can decline this replay runoff.
If discussing prevention, either team may use a remaining charged timeout.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: After an offensive act illegally conserves time with the clock running after the two-minute warning, can the defense decline the usual ten-second runoff?
answer_rubric: Answers yes; defense may decline the runoff.
Does not conflate it with the replay runoff that neither team may decline.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: The ball reaches the line to gain while the play is live, then becomes dead short of it in offensive possession. Is merely reaching the line while live sufficient for a new series?
answer_rubric: Answers no; ordinary new-series measurement uses the forward-most point when the ball becomes dead.
Does not invent a forward-progress exception absent from this corpus.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: A receiver controls the pass, gets two feet inbounds, and maintains control long enough to perform a football act without actually performing one. Must a later loss on ground contact make the pass incomplete?
answer_rubric: Answers no; sufficient time to perform a football act is an alternative to actually performing one.
Once all catch requirements are complete, maintaining control through the ground is not required.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: A backward pass first hits the ground behind the point where it was thrown. Does hitting the ground end the play?
answer_rubric: Answers no; a backward pass remains live after hitting the ground and either team may recover and advance it.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: A field-goal kick hits the ground before going over the crossbar between the uprights. Does passing between the uprights make it a scoring field goal?
answer_rubric: Answers no; a scoring field goal must not first touch the ground.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: Does the game clock run during the scrimmage down used for a try after a touchdown?
answer_rubric: Answers no; the game clock does not run during the try.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.

cases.question: A runner possesses the ball when it breaks the plane of the opponent goal line and then loses it. When did the ball become dead under the supplied scoring rule?
answer_rubric: The touchdown requirement is satisfied while possessing the ball at the plane; the ball becomes dead then.
Does not impose receiver catch requirements on a runner.
Contains no other material rule claim that contradicts or exceeds the supplied corpus evidence.
